1.explanation: In connection-pool.js, ConnectionPool._initializeConnections groups records by origin and then reads serverResponseTimeByOrigin.get(origin) or falls back to DEFAULT_SERVER_RESPONSE_TIME (30 ms). Data URIs have a securityOrigin of 'data' and aren’t added to serverResponseTimeByOrigin, so they receive the 30 ms default. To fix this, _initializeConnections must detect the 'data' scheme (or empty origin) and override responseTime to 0 for data URIs rather than using DEFAULT_SERVER_RESPONSE_TIME.
1.bug_scenario: When you feed a data-URI resource into the Lighthouse network simulator, it still picks up the default serverResponseTime (≈30 ms) even though data URIs are local and should never incur server latency. In the screenshot you can see additionalRtt is 0 (as expected) but responseTime is 30 for a data:image/png;base64… request.

2.explanation: The bug stems from ConnectionPool._initializeConnections in connection-pool.js, which does `serverResponseTimeByOrigin.get(origin) || DEFAULT_SERVER_RESPONSE_TIME`. Since data URIs have a ‘data’ securityOrigin that’s never populated in the options map, they always fall back to the 30 ms default. Those defaults themselves originate from Simulator.getOptions and are passed into _initializeConnectionPool (and ultimately ConnectionPool), so both the Simulator’s option-building (getOptions/_initializeConnectionPool) and the ConnectionPool’s default fallback logic need adjustment to special-case data URIs and set their serverResponseTime to zero.
2.bug_scenario: When feeding a data-URI resource into the Lantern network simulator, it still picks up the default server response time (≈30 ms) even though data URIs are local and should incur zero server latency. In the screenshot you can see additionalRtt is 0 (correct) but responseTime is 30 for a data:image/png;base64… request because the ConnectionPool code falls back to DEFAULT_SERVER_RESPONSE_TIME whenever an origin has no explicit entry in the serverResponseTimeByOrigin map.
